html:
The Otomí are an Indigenous people of the central Mexican highlands, who speak Otomanguean languages. The map shows an Otomí area in the 1500s around Querétaro and southern Guanajuato, on the northern edge of the farming world.

Otomí had lived in central Mexico for thousands of years. Their town of Xaltocan was a power before the Aztecs, and later many Otomí lived as subjects of the Aztec Triple Alliance. After the fall of Tenochtitlan many sided with Spain. Otomí leaders founded Querétaro around 1531, and Otomí settlers and soldiers held the frontier during the Chichimeca War.

Today they are one of the larger Indigenous peoples of Mexico, living in a broken band of territory from Guanajuato to Veracruz. See also Hñähñu (Otomí) on the modern map.
